summary: Auth token rotation + tracing baggage growth leading to header blowup and streaming stalls
description: Customer reports repeated long-running streaming requests that either stall mid-stream (no bytes forwarded for 10-40s) or terminate with downstream 5xx/503. Issue coincided with a spike in client-side auth token rotation and enhanced tracing baggage being sent by the customer's SDK. Affects long completions (>60s).
impact: Multiple production inference sessions for Acme Analytics experienced increased TTFB and several hard disconnects impacting their real-time analytics pipeline. Estimated 12% of streaming requests in the window failed or timed out; customer reported user-visible failures in dashboards. Customer is on a dedicated pool and expects low-latency streaming.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use Acme Analytics SDK configured with tracing baggage that appends per-retry metadata and rotates the auth token every ~30s.
2) Start a long streaming completion (min 90s of generation) against the hosted API endpoint in prod/us-west.
3) Observe headers on repeated upstream connections grow over time; after several re-auth cycles the combined header size exceeds proxy buffer thresholds and streaming data stalls or the connection is reset.
4) Reproduce more reliably by toggling repeated token rotation and adding a 64KB tracing baggage payload.
logs_and_traces:
- Edge request IDs: req-20260312-az2-773e, req-20260312-az2-88b9
- ALB logs show Idle timeout resets at 30s for connections where no bytes were forwarded: ALB 503, target: 504 on some flows.
- APIGW/nginx proxy error log: 'upstream prematurely closed connection' and 'request header too large' in ~25% of affected sessions.
- Observability traces show repeated upstream reconnects with cumulative header_size growing from ~6KB to ~78KB over the session.
- Customer provided HAR and SDK logs showing token rotation and baggage append per retry loop.
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis was a serving-runtime KV cache warmup causing stalls; telemetry did not show CPU/GPU saturation.
- Correlation found between sessions that rotated auth tokens frequently and sessions with stalls.
- Packet captures at the edge show that client-side SDK is appending 'x-trace-baggage' on each retry instead of overwriting, causing linear growth.
- Nginx (API GW) default proxy_buffer_size and large_client_header_buffers were exceeded; proxy buffering enabled caused delayed flushes and coalescing behavior that increased TTFB.
- ALB/ELB idle timeout configured at 30s interacted poorly with proxy buffering: when proxy held on to buffered body/headers for flush, ALB considered connection idle and reset.
- Reproduced internally by running the SDK in a loop with token rotation; confirmed header growth and the same ALB/nginx errors.
root_cause: Client SDK behavior (auth rotation + append-mode tracing baggage) caused request headers to grow beyond the API GW/nginx buffer limits. With proxy_buffering enabled the proxy delayed downstream flushes, which together with ALB's 30s idle cutoff resulted in mid-stream stalls and connection resets. Not a serving-runtime GPU resource issue.
workaround:
1) Short-term: Instruct customer to turn off per-retry baggage append (set SDK to overwrite baggage header) and reduce token rotation frequency.
2) On Redwood edge: temporarily increase nginx large_client_header_buffers and proxy_buffer_size for the affected APIGW fleet in us-west for the dedicated account, and set proxy_request_buffering off for streaming routes.
3) Increase ALB idle timeout to 60s for the affected target group while mitigation is in place.
resolution:
- Customer applied SDK change to overwrite tracing baggage instead of append; confirmed immediate reduction in header growth.
- Platform change deployed: PR #4512 increased nginx large_client_header_buffers and disabled proxy_request_buffering on streaming proxy v2 for the dedicated tenant routes (rolled to 3 pods in us-west, feature flag gated).
- ALB idle timeout for the customer's target group increased to 60s as a safety net.
- Post-deploy monitoring for 48h showed streaming failure rate decreased from ~12% to <1% and TTFB returned to normal baselines.
follow_up_actions:
- SDK team to publish a patch and release notes recommending overwrite-mode for tracing baggage and guidance on token rotation (GH PR: https://github.com/acme-analytics/sdk/pull/98).
- Platform: add defensive header-size rate-limiting and telemetry alert when combined request header > 32KB.
- Ops: update runbook for streaming incidents to include header-size checks and adjust ALB timeouts.
- Engineering: investigate optional early drop of oversized tracing baggage at edge for long-streaming sessions.
- Create a Confluence postmortem page and link to incident timeline (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/SUP-99816+Postmortem).
